claims.text: A thin molybdenum-based interlayer can act as an effective buffer between W and CuCrZr.
Refining and directionally orienting the Mo interlayer microstructure improves its buffering effectiveness.
A Mo interlayer reduces the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer improves interfacial bonding between W and CuCrZr.
Minor alloying additions can tailor the thermal expansion and mechanical properties of bulk molybdenum.
Vacuum deposition or directional solidification can produce a controlled-thickness Mo interlayer with a refined, aligned microstructure.
A refined and directionally aligned Mo grain structure can mediate crystallographic mismatch at W/Mo and Mo/CuCrZr interfaces.
A refined and directionally aligned Mo grain structure can mediate thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
The intermediate thermal expansion of Mo reduces thermal stresses in a W/Mo/CuCrZr joint.
The Mo interlayer provides a gradual transition in lattice parameters between W and CuCrZr.
A refined or directionally solidified Mo microstructure enhances mechanical adhesion.
A refined or directionally solidified Mo microstructure minimizes detrimental interfacial-phase formation.
Suppressing detrimental interfacial phases helps preserve bonding and durability during high heat flux and irradiation.

Compared with direct W/CuCrZr bonding, a Mo interlayer improves interfacial adhesion, reduces thermal-stress accumulation, and stabilizes the interface microstructure under extreme operating conditions.
Direct bonding of W and CuCrZr typically produces high residual stresses because of their large thermal-expansion mismatch.
An excessively thick or improperly processed Mo interlayer may limit the interlayer's benefit.
Long-term irradiation may destabilize phases in the W/Mo/CuCrZr interlayer system.
